capabilities: Visualize tag co-occurrence as a heatmap and tag intersections as a lattice
Render note neighborhoods as nested icon grids and containment bubbles
Filter the graph by Bases files, folders, tags, and frontmatter searches
Bind note attributes to visual channels with a declarative encoding engine
Flag graph complexity, co-occurrence gaps, and similar unlinked note pairs
disambiguation: Not a tag editor or tag-cleanup tool; it visualizes tag-note relationships and only suggests, not performs, tag refactoring.
extras: The containment/Euler family modes are labeled experimental and work best on desktop; requires Obsidian 1.5.0+; plugin is listed as not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; runs fully locally with no network requests.
problem: Obsidian's graph view is a single force-directed layout that turns into a hairball when notes are tagged in deeply overlapping ways, and it offers no tag-specific structural views.
summary: Visualization plugin that explores tag-note structure in Bases vaults with four view modes: icon gallery, intersection lattice, co-occurrence heatmap, and BubbleSets.
